objective: Derive exact all-length fixed-complement stem responses, minimum two-port support and a precisely bounded failed deletion, without asserting universal coverage of remaining minimum obstructions. Both C1 p values are handled; C2 is untouched.

atomic_claims.text: The complete pinned-stem state space has signed displacements 0>=x0>=...>=xm>=s-6, so its exact root response is 10+s through16 for every length.
For both C1 p1 and p14, fixed-complement O filling is possible exactly at offsets s0 or1; minimum total changed support is m+4, unbounded with length. At s1 the filling state is unique.

Reverse tail preparations followed by the explicit synchronous two-port fork update construct the same actual coloring and terminate with an O fill; induced-tree response messages retain argmin witnesses and fixed vertex identities.
For an exterior set containing k of the O ports, the correct cut count is n+6-2k-2c-d. The stem support contains two ports and has m+6 leaving incidences after adjoining O.

Offsets s2 through6 prohibit every internal fixed-complement repair and provide failed lifts for deletion of precisely O plus the stem. This is not a certificate against other absorptions or root coloring.

assumptions: Every support and cut incidence, actual fixed color, and exterior vertex identity is retained. The stem is induced and has exactly the listed pins.
Four exterior ports are distinct. Equal-colored cut neighbors can coincide only consistently with simplicity and the degree bound.
The all-length colored-stem theorem is conditional; it is not a theorem that every remaining minimum obstruction contains such a stem.
risks: All four whole classes and both admitted obligations remain open. No universal minimum-obstruction recoloring or strict net-smaller replacement has been proved.
The finite controls have prescribed pins and low-degree fixed vertices. They do not meet all unpinned all-target hypotheses or all minimum-counterexample restrictions.
Unbounded minimum total support is not an unbounded per-step atomic requirement; the proof gives single-vertex preparations followed by a four-point step.
The negative deletion certificate fixes exactly the specified complement; changing its terminal pin gives a full coloring, so it cannot be a root or all-absorption counterexample.
